problem_statement.title: default_build_sdist produces sdists rooted at build_dir's name instead of {name}-{version}
problem_statement.body:
## Problem

The [sdist specification](https://packaging.python.org/en/latest/specifications/source-distribution-format/#source-distribution-file-format) requires that a source distribution contain exactly one top-level directory named `{name}-{version}`.

When a package sets `build_dir` in its package settings (the monorepo-subdirectory case), `default_build_sdist` produces a tarball rooted at the *build directory's* name instead. The filename is correct; only the directory inside is wrong.

For example, a package `mlserver-xgboost` whose sources live in `runtimes/xgboost/` yields `mlserver-xgboost-1.7.1.tar.gz` that unpacks into `xgboost/`.

## Cause

`default_build_sdist` tars from `build_dir` using the parent as the archive prefix:

https://github.com/python-wheel-build/fromager/blob/4eeb0f415c237578b2b970c516bbf2cee75b409f/src/fromager/sources.py#L549-L553

`tar_reproducible` then computes each entry as `arcname = os.path.relpath(fn, prefix)`:

https://github.com/python-wheel-build/fromager/blob/4eeb0f415c237578b2b970c516bbf2cee75b409f/src/fromager/tarballs.py#L58

So when `build_dir` is `<sdist_root_dir>/runtimes/xgboost`, `prefix` becomes `<sdist_root_dir>/runtimes` and every path is rooted at `xgboost/`. When `build_dir` is unset it equals `sdist_root_dir`, the prefix is its parent, and the root comes out correct — which is why this only affects packages that configure `build_dir`.

## Reproducer

No network or package settings required; it calls `default_build_sdist` directly.

```python
"""Reproducer: sdist top-level directory is build_dir's name, not {name}-{version}."""
import pathlib, tarfile, tempfile, types
from packaging.requirements import Requirement
from packaging.version import Version
from fromager import sources


def build(subdir: str | None) -> list[str]:
    tmp = pathlib.Path(tempfile.mkdtemp())
    sdist_root = tmp / "mypkg-1.0"
    build_dir = sdist_root / subdir if subdir else sdist_root
    build_dir.mkdir(parents=True)
    (build_dir / "setup.py").write_text("from setuptools import setup; setup()\n")
    out = tmp / "sdists-builds"
    out.mkdir()
    sdist = sources.default_build_sdist(
        types.SimpleNamespace(sdists_builds=out),  # ctx
        {},                                        # extra_environ
        Requirement("mypkg"),                      # req
        Version("1.0"),                            # version
        sdist_root,                                # sdist_root_dir
        None,                                      # build_env (unused here)
        build_dir,                                 # build_dir
    )
    with tarfile.open(sdist) as tar:
        return sorted({n.split("/")[0] for n in tar.getnames()})


print(f"build_dir unset (== sdist_root_dir) -> {build(None)}")
print(f"build_dir = 'python'               -> {build('python')}")
print(f"expected in both cases             -> ['mypkg-1.0']")
```

Run with `uv run --with-editable . python repro.py`:

```
build_dir unset (== sdist_root_dir) -> ['mypkg-1.0']
build_dir = 'python'               -> ['python']
expected in both cases             -> ['mypkg-1.0']
```

## Impact

Installers tolerate the layout — `pip` and `uv` build these sdists without complaint — so this does not break installs. It does affect anything that relies on the documented structure:

**Name collisions between unrelated projects.** The root directory is no longer unique per package, so distinct projects can produce sdists that unpack over each other. In one published index built with fromager, four unrelated projects (`ctranslate2`, `flatbuffers`, `tacozip`, `triton`) all emit sdists rooted at `python/`. Extracting two of them into the same directory silently loses one:

```
after flatbuffers-25.12.19.tar.gz: out/python/PKG-INFO says Name: flatbuffers
after ctranslate2-4.8.1.tar.gz:    out/python/PKG-INFO says Name: ctranslate2
what survived: python
```

No error is raised. Workflows that unpack a set of sdists into a common tree — source auditing, license scanning, vendoring, offline mirroring — drop packages here rather than failing loudly.

**Identity mismatch.** `PKG-INFO` inside the archive carries the correct `Name:` while the directory it sits in does not, so tools that infer the project from the directory name disagree with tools that read the metadata.

Same published index: 72 of 3,384 sdists have a top-level directory that is not `{name}-{version}`. Observed roots include `python/`, `xgboost/`, `sklearn/`, `lightgbm/`, `onnx/`, `core/`, `common/`, `tabular/`, `timeseries/`, `ogx_api/`.

This may also matter for #1311, which proposes unpacking the generated sdist and building the wheel from it — that pipeline would have to special-case a root directory that isn't `{name}-{version}`.

## Suggested fix

Root the archive entries at `{name}-{version}` regardless of where `build_dir` points, rather than deriving the prefix from `build_dir.parent`. `tar_reproducible` already takes the prefix as a parameter, so this could be an explicit arcname root rather than a path-relative computation.

problem_statement.title: Windows: a hook outside the working tree is not found from a repository under %TEMP% (Git Bash mounts it as /tmp)
problem_statement.body:
> This issue was written by Claude Code, an AI agent, on behalf of the account owner.

### What happens

On Windows, with a `core.hooksPath` outside the working tree (for example a global `~/.config/git/hooks` holding a `pre-commit` hook), `IndexFile.commit` fails for any repository under the user's temporary directory:

```
git.exc.HookExecutionError: Hook('C:\Users\<user>\.config\git\hooks\pre-commit') failed due to: exit code(127)
  cmdline: C:\Users\<user>\.config\git\hooks\pre-commit
  stderr: '/usr/bin/bash: ../../../../../.config/git/hooks/pre-commit: No such file or directory
'
```

The same hook runs fine from a repository elsewhere (e.g. under `C:\data`). Test suites that create their repositories in `tempfile` directories hit it on every commit; on this machine that includes GitPython's own hook tests in `test/test_index.py`.

### Reproduce

Windows 11, Git for Windows 2.50.1, Python 3.14; GitPython 3.1.62 and current `main` (563cb1f3):

```sh
git config --global core.hooksPath ~/.config/git/hooks   # a directory holding an executable pre-commit hook
```

```python
import tempfile
from pathlib import Path

import git

repo = git.Repo.init(Path(tempfile.mkdtemp(), "repo"))
repo.index.commit("probe")  # HookExecutionError, exit code 127
```

### Cause

`run_commit_hook` passes Bash the hook's path relative to the working tree, `os.path.relpath(hp, index.repo.working_dir)`, computed on the Windows side: from `C:\Users\<user>\AppData\Local\Temp\tmpXXXX\repo`, five `..` reach `C:\Users\<user>`. But Git for Windows mounts the user's temporary directory as `/tmp` (`none /tmp usertemp binary,posix=0,noacl 0 0` in its `/etc/fstab`), so Bash starts in `/tmp/tmpXXXX/repo`, where the same five `..` lead to `/`:

```console
$ cd /tmp/tmpXXXX/repo && ls ../../../../../.config/git/hooks/pre-commit
ls: cannot access '../../../../../.config/git/hooks/pre-commit': No such file or directory
```

A relative path is only valid in Bash while it does not cross a mount point. A hook inside the working tree never does; one outside it can. The relative path was introduced in 9bc287a2 so that a hook outside the working tree could run at all; a working tree under a mount point was not covered.

### Possible fix

Keep the relative path for a hook inside the working tree. When the relative path leaves the working tree, pass the absolute path in POSIX form (`C:/...`), as is already done for a hook on another drive, if the Bash is Git for Windows' own or one found on `PATH`: both accept it. The bare `bash.exe` fallback, which may be the WSL launcher, would keep the relative path. A PR with this change follows.

problem_statement.title: [BUG] key_value_replace still corrupts notebook .py files that parse as a YAML mapping (follow-up to #890)
problem_statement.body:
### Library Version

1.2.0 (also reproduced on 1.4.0)

### Python Version

3.14.8

### Operating System

Linux

### Authentication Method

Service principal (secret)

### What is the problem?

#890 / #889 fixed `key_value_replace` corrupting notebook `.py` files by making `check_valid_yaml_content()` return True only when the content parses as a mapping or sequence. That covers notebooks whose uncommented code parses as a plain scalar, but not ones whose uncommented code happens to parse as a mapping.

Every notebook structural line (`# Fabric notebook source`, `# META`, `# CELL`, `# MAGIC`) is a YAML comment. If the remaining Python is something like:

```python
for p in ["a", "b"]:
    spark.conf.set(p, globals()[p])
```

YAML reads it as `{'for p in ["a", "b"]': 'spark.conf.set(p, globals()[p])'}`, a mapping. The file passes `check_valid_yaml_content()`, and `replace_key_value()` then returns `yaml.dump(data)` even though the `find_key` matched nothing. All comment lines are dropped, including the prologue and cell markers, and Fabric rejects the result.

We hit this with a notebook whose parameters cell was commented out and whose other cells were all `%%sql` (`# MAGIC` lines), so a single `for` loop was the only uncommented code. A `key_value_replace` entry filtered by `item_type: Notebook` (meant for `.schedules`) was enough to trigger it. Git Sync of the same commit works.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Add a `key_value_replace` entry to `parameter.yml` that applies to Notebook items without a `file_path` filter, for example:
   ```yaml
   key_value_replace:
     - find_key: $.schedules[*].enabled
       replace_value:
         dev: false
       item_type: Notebook
   ```
2. Add a notebook whose only uncommented code parses as a YAML mapping, for example the `for` loop above, with all other cells being `%%sql` or markdown.
3. Deploy.

Minimal repro without deploying (fabric-cicd 1.4.0):

```python
from fabric_cicd._common._check_utils import check_valid_yaml_content
from fabric_cicd._parameter._utils import replace_key_value

notebook = """# Fabric notebook source

# METADATA ********************

# META {
# META   "kernel_info": {
# META     "name": "synapse_pyspark"
# META   }
# META }

# CELL ********************

for p in ["a", "b"]:
    spark.conf.set(p, globals()[p])

# METADATA ********************

# META {
# META   "language": "python",
# META   "language_group": "synapse_pyspark"
# META }
"""

class Ws:
    environment = "dev"

print("check_valid_yaml_content:", check_valid_yaml_content(notebook))
param = {"find_key": "$.schedules[*].enabled", "replace_value": {"dev": False}}
print(replace_key_value(Ws(), param, notebook, "dev", is_yaml=True))
```

Output:

```
check_valid_yaml_content: True
for p in ["a", "b"]: spark.conf.set(p, globals()[p])
```

### Expected behavior

The notebook is published unchanged, since it is not a YAML file and the `find_key` does not match anything in it.

### Actual behavior

The notebook content is replaced with a YAML dump of its uncommented code, and publishing fails:

```
Failed to publish Notebook '<name>': Operation failed. Error Code: NB_CLR_NotebookServiceApiException. Error Message: "Convert data from py to ipynb failed. Detail: PyToIPynb: the py format is not correct - The py content is not supported - prologue is invalid. Expected prologue: # Fabric notebook source\r" (Crud) (HTTP 400) Operation: Import
```

### Is there an ideal solution?

Either of these would fix it, and together they would also cover other non-YAML files that happen to parse as YAML:

1. In `replace_key_value()`, return the original `content` unchanged when `jsonpath_expr.find(data)` finds no matches, instead of always re-serializing. Re-dumping also drops comments and reformats real YAML files that had no matches.
2. Decide JSON/YAML handling by file extension (`.json`, `.yml`, `.yaml`, `.schedules`, `.platform`, etc.) rather than by whether the content happens to parse, so `.py`, `.kql`, `.sql` and similar files are never treated as YAML.

### Additional context, screenshots, logs, error output, etc

- Previous report and fix: #890, #889. The test added in #889 uses `print("hello world")` as the only code, which parses as a scalar, so the mapping case isn't covered.
- Workaround: make sure the notebook has uncommented code that doesn't parse as a YAML mapping. Scoping the `key_value_replace` entry with a `file_path` filter so it never touches `.py` files should also avoid it.

 * ``@``/``dot`` against a sparse constant no longer scales with the total number of variables in the model: each chunk of the sparse product now runs on only the variables it uses, which removes several seconds of allocation overhead on models with millions of variables. (`#990 <https://github.com/PyPSA/linopy/pull/990>`__)
 * Deprecated in favour of ``Model(sparse=True)``, each with a ``FutureWarning`` and to be removed with the legacy semantics: ``Model(freeze_constraints=...)`` and the ``Model.freeze_constraints`` setter, ``groupby(...).sum(sparse=...)`` and ``linopy.options["sparse_groupby"]``. They keep their current behaviour until then, except that ``@`` ignores ``sparse_groupby``, and netcdf files that store ``freeze_constraints`` still load. (`#976 <https://github.com/PyPSA/linopy/issues/976>`__)
 * Adding a frozen constraint from a sparse expression no longer copies the lhs matrix when every row stays active, and picks the mask and the row scaling at the active rows without expanding them over the full coordinate grid. This roughly halves the peak memory of ``add_constraints`` on a sparse model. (`#977 <https://github.com/PyPSA/linopy/issues/977>`__)

On a model with 2M variables this cuts the freeze of the nodal balance from about 465 to 185 ms and its peak memory from 1.74 GB to 0.25 GB. problem_statement.title: Faster CSR kernel: merge in one pass, row gather for reorderings
problem_statement.body:
> [!NOTE]
> The following content was generated by AI.

## Describe the feature you'd like to see

Child of #972 (phase 2, PR 7). Internal changes only, with no change to the API or semantics.

Three places in `linopy/csr.py` do more work than they need to:

1. `_try_csr_merge` (`linopy/expressions.py:3767-3769`) folds the operands pairwise through `CSRLinearExpression.added` (`linopy/csr.py:575-594`). With n operands, the early terms go through COO and sorting n-1 times.
2. `reindexed` (`linopy/csr.py:537-560`) goes through COO and sorting, even when the reindex only reorders rows. A transpose or a `sel` with unique labels are examples. A direct `csr[rows]` gives the same result.
3. `aggregated` (`linopy/csr.py:442-458`) builds `rows[coo.coords[0]]` as int64. `coo_to_csr` (`linopy/csr.py:719-729`) then copies it back to int32.

```python
import numpy as np, pandas as pd, linopy
linopy.options["semantics"] = "v1"
i, t = pd.RangeIndex(2000, name="i"), pd.RangeIndex(720, name="t")
m = linopy.Model(sparse=True)
x = m.add_variables(0, 1, coords=[i, t], name="x")
g = pd.Series(np.r_[np.zeros(800, int), np.arange(1200) % 199 + 1], index=i, name="g")
e = [x.groupby(g).sum() * k for k in (1, 2, 3)]
e[0] + e[1] + e[2]  # about 130 ms, pairwise
```

### Proposed direction

- Add a classmethod that merges all operands in one COO concatenation and one `coo_to_csr` call, and call it from `_try_csr_merge`. Keep the absence rule (a cell absent in any operand is absent in the result) and keep explicit zeros (`linopy/csr.py:12-16`).
- In `reindexed`, use a row gather when every target label exists and the map is a permutation.
- Index with int32 rows in `aggregated` to avoid the int64 copy.
- Tests: the existing merge and reindex tests, plus merges of 3 or more operands with absent cells.

<details>
<summary>Measurements (scratch benchmarks)</summary>

| case | current | prototype |
|---|---|---|
| chain of 3 scaled operands, merged | 181 ms (pairwise) | 86 ms (one COO pass) |
| reindex to a transposed grid | 19-31 ms | 4-18 ms (`csr[rows]`) |

</details>

problem_statement.title: os.path.sameopenfile doesn't work with files in the fake filesystem
problem_statement.body:
**Describe the bug**
`os.path.sameopenfile` raises `OSError: [Errno 9] Bad file descriptor` for two descriptors opened on the same file in the fake filesystem. `os.fstat` works on the same descriptors.

Expected: `os.path.sameopenfile(fd1, fd2)` returns `True`.

```
os.fstat(fd1).st_size             -> 0                                         (correct)
os.path.sameopenfile(fd1, fd2)    -> OSError: [Errno 9] Bad file descriptor    (expected True)
```

I see the same under simulated Linux, macOS and Windows.

**How To Reproduce**
Run on a POSIX host:

```python
import os
from pyfakefs.fake_filesystem_unittest import Patcher

with Patcher() as p:
    os.makedirs('/d')
    open('/d/a', 'w').close()
    fd1 = os.open('/d/a', os.O_RDONLY)
    fd2 = os.open('/d/a', os.O_RDONLY)
    print(os.fstat(fd1).st_size)
    print(os.path.sameopenfile(fd1, fd2))
```

**Your environment**
```
macOS-27.0-arm64-arm-64bit-Mach-O
Python 3.14.7 (main, Aug  5 2026, 10:29:49) [Clang 21.0.0 (clang-2100.1.1.101)]
pyfakefs 6.2.0
ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'pytest'
```

problem_statement.title: Enums with custom `__init__` cannot be imported under mutmut: `KeyError: '_mutmut_orig'`
problem_statement.body:
My project has enums with a custom `__init__`, and `mutmut run` stops at the stats run because the mutated module cannot be imported.

`Enum` calls `__init__` once per member while the class is still being created, before the trampoline table of its methods is assigned after the class body. `__new__` is already in `NEVER_MUTATE_FUNCTION_NAMES` for that reason.

Skipping `__init__` and `_generate_next_value_` on an enum class the same way works for me. Shall I submit a PR?

## Reproducer

mutmut 3.8.0, pytest 9.1.1, Python 3.15, `mutmut run`:
```
File ".../mutmut/mutation/trampoline.py", line 75, in trampoline
  orig_func = mutants_dict["_mutmut_orig"]
KeyError: '_mutmut_orig'
ERROR tests/test_color.py - KeyError: '_mutmut_orig'
failed to collect stats. runner returned 2
```

`src/color.py`:
```python
from enum import Enum


class Color(Enum):
    RED = 1

    def __init__(self, value):
        self.label = f"c{value}"
```

`tests/test_color.py`:
```python
from color import Color


def test_label():
    assert Color.RED.label == "c1"
```

`pyproject.toml`:
```toml
[tool.mutmut]
source_paths = ["src"]

[tool.pytest.ini_options]
pythonpath = ["src"]
```

diff --git a/CHANGELOG.md b/CHANGELOG.md
index 56ca77c6..cb1393bc 100644
--- a/CHANGELOG.md
+++ b/CHANGELOG.md
@@ -24,6 +24,7 @@ Types of changes:
 ### Removed
 
 ### Fixed
+- Fixed bare OpenQASM expression statements raising `AttributeError` or `KeyError`. Their values are now evaluated and discarded, and unknown gate errors name the gate using the original source line. ([#388](https://github.com/qBraid/pyqasm/issues/388))
 - Fixed qubit register ranges dropping their final qubit during unrolling. Endpoints are now inclusive for gates, aliases, barriers, and measurements. Code using an exclusive upper bound must lower it by one, for example `q[0:1]` instead of `q[0:2]` to select two qubits. ([#432](https://github.com/qBraid/pyqasm/issues/432))
 - Fixed `cs` and `csdg` from `stdgates.inc` being rejected during unrolling. They now decompose to controlled phase shifts. ([#439](https://github.com/qBraid/pyqasm/issues/439))
 - Fixed Clifford+T rebasing for exact `rx`, `ry`, and `rz` rotations at multiples of π/4. These gates now decompose instead of disappearing, while angles outside the exact basis raise `RebaseError` instead of producing an incorrect result. ([#428](https://github.com/qBraid/pyqasm/issues/428))

+    def _visit_expression_statement(
+        self, statement: qasm3_ast.ExpressionStatement
+    ) -> list[qasm3_ast.Statement]:
+        """Visit an expression statement in an OpenPulse block.
+
+        OpenPulse functions retain their specialized validation and output.
+        Other expressions use the main visitor's evaluator and discard their
+        value.
+
+        Args:
+            statement (ExpressionStatement): The expression statement to visit.
+
+        Returns:
+            list[Statement]: Statements produced while evaluating the expression.
+        """
+        expression = statement.expression
+        pulse_functions = {
+            *OPENPULSE_FRAME_FUNCTION_MAP,
+            *OPENPULSE_WAVEFORM_FUNCTION_MAP,
+            *OPENPULSE_CAPTURE_FUNCTION_MAP,
+            # Keep these names in sync with the special cases in _visit_function_call.
+            "get_phase",
+            "get_frequency",
+            "newframe",
+            "play",
+        }
+        if (
+            isinstance(expression, qasm3_ast.FunctionCall)
+            and expression.name.name in pulse_functions
+        ):
+            _, statements = self._visit_function_call(expression)
+            return statements  # type: ignore[return-value]
+        _, statements = Qasm3ExprEvaluator.evaluate_expression(expression)
+        return statements
+
     def visit_statement(
         self, statement: qasm3_ast.Statement | qasm3_ast.Pragma
     ) -> list[qasm3_ast.Statement]:
@@ -789,7 +824,7 @@ def visit_statement(
         visit_map = {

problem_statement.title: Bare expression statements crash with `AttributeError` instead of raising `ValidationError`
problem_statement.body:
## Limitation

An expression followed by a semicolon is a syntactically valid OpenQASM 3 statement — the
[classical types](https://openqasm.com/versions/3.1/language/classical.html) chapter uses this form throughout to
illustrate operator results, for example under
[Integers](https://openqasm.com/versions/3.1/language/classical.html#integers) and
[Angles](https://openqasm.com/versions/3.1/language/classical.html#angles).

`pyqasm` reaches these statements and dereferences `.name` on the expression node. For any
non-`Identifier` expression this raises an `AttributeError` that escapes the public API. The
same dereference fails for an undeclared gate applied to zero qubits.

## Example QASM failure

Straight from the spec's Integers section:

```python
import pyqasm

m = pyqasm.loads('''
OPENQASM 3.0;
int[32] a = 2;
int[32] b = 3;

a * b;   // 6
b / a;   // 1
b % a;   // 1
''')
m.validate()
```

```
AttributeError: 'BinaryExpression' object has no attribute 'name'
```

The spec's Angles section fails identically:

```qasm
OPENQASM 3.0;
angle[4] a = 7 * (pi / 8);
angle[4] b = pi / 8;
a + b;
// AttributeError: 'BinaryExpression' object has no attribute 'name'
```

And the gate-application example in
[Applying gates](https://openqasm.com/versions/3.1/language/gates.html#applying-gates):

```qasm
OPENQASM 3.0;
g1 q1;
// AttributeError: 'str' object has no attribute 'name'
```

## Change Requested

1. Never surface an `AttributeError` from a statement `pyqasm` does not handle. Every
   unhandled statement or expression form must raise `ValidationError` carrying the source
   span.
2. Decide and document the semantics of a bare expression statement. It has no effect on the
   quantum program, so the reasonable options are to evaluate and discard it, or to reject it
   with a clear message such as `"Expression statement has no effect"`. Either is acceptable;
   the current crash is not.
3. An undefined gate identifier must report the undefined name, not fail on an attribute
   lookup.

## Implementation Details

- The root cause is the visitor's dispatch table in `src/pyqasm/visitor.py:193`:

  ```python
  qasm3_ast.ExpressionStatement: lambda x: self._visit_function_call(x.expression),
  ```

  Every expression statement is assumed to be a function call, so `_visit_function_call`
  dereferences `x.expression.name` — which exists on an `Identifier` but not on a
  `BinaryExpression`, a `UnaryExpression`, an `IndexExpression`, or a literal.
- The fix is to branch on the expression type before dispatching: route `FunctionCall` to
  `_visit_function_call` and give every other form the chosen behaviour from point 2 above.
  The generic fallback at `visitor.py:3492` already raises the correct error shape and can be
  reused.
- The `'str' object has no attribute 'name'` variant comes from the gate-operation path, where
  the operation name has already been reduced to a string before the undefined-gate check
  runs. Reorder so the lookup failure is reported first.
- Add a defensive `try/except (AttributeError, TypeError)` around the visitor's top-level
  dispatch that re-raises as `ValidationError` with the statement span. This converts any
  remaining internal slips in the tree into the documented error type — a cheap safety net
  beyond this specific fix.
- Tests: `tests/qasm3/test_validation.py` — assert `ValidationError` (not `AttributeError`)
  for a bare binary expression, a bare function call, a bare identifier, and an undefined gate
  with zero and with one qubit operand.

problem_statement.title: [Console] - Misleading warnings when adding a catalog with aqua add
problem_statement.body:
## Description:

When adding a catalog in editable mode on a fresh installation (empty ~/.aqua/catalogs), the command prints two warnings right after the catalog is installed:

```
$ aqua add obs -e ~/Climate-DT-catalog/catalogs/obs
Adding the AQUA catalog obs
Installing catalog in editable mode from .../Climate-DT-catalog/catalogs/obs to ~/.aqua
ConfigCatalog :: WARNING  -> No available catalogs found
ShowCatalog :: WARNING  -> No catalogs available to scan
```

The catalog is correctly installed (aqua list shows it), but the warnings suggest something went wrong, which can be confusing for new users.
